claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch now on a qualified basis because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and a 7% monitored rollout with rollback capability is sufficient so long as the unresolved developer-support migration weakness is explicitly documented.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the named launch use-case limitation is disclosed in the launch model card or certification record, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows a reviewed and approved risk acceptance that specifically covers developer-support migration exposure before launch, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows the rollout now excludes the affected use case from exposure, the verdict could improve.
Absent one of those predicates, certifying the model now is not fully supported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual certification or model-card artifact showing the unresolved developer-support migration limitation is disclosed for launch.
Provide an approved risk acceptance that specifically names the exposed developer-support migration segment, if disclosure is not the path being used.
Provide evidence that the initial rollout excludes the affected use case, if that control has changed since the cited rollout plan.
specific_concerns: The affected developer-support migration segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The risk acceptance is not approved: the approver line is blank.
The draft risk acceptance does not address the exposed developer-support migration segment.
The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The stricter policy text says rollout controls mitigate only if they exclude the affected use case or include reviewed risk acceptance; neither condition is satisfied by the evidence provided.
There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has actually been completed in the certification artifact.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable, rather than only conditionally supportable after documented disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
That rollout monitoring and rollback meaningfully close the policy gap while the affected use case remains exposed.
That the packet's proposed qualified certification record already satisfies the policy threshold; no admissible artifact shows that disclosure is in place.
